# Enter-to-end-turn browser wait exceeds the 60 s hook above ~2x CPU oversubscription

## Headline

The `turn to advance after end-of-turn presentation` wait in
`tests/main-street/MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts` is already at the largest
budget the 60 s browser hook permits (40 000 ms = 16 000 ms cap + 24 000 ms
margin + 20 000 ms boot = 60 000 ms), yet it fails at ≈2× CPU oversubscription
because the bounded end-of-turn deferral is re-polled on Phaser's clamped game
clock, so the forced day start is detected late. **Decision: make the
deferral's safety cap starvation-proof** — one extracted helper whose deadline
and re-poll run on wall clock, enforced even while the page is not painting
(producer, Q1 = C, Q2 = 1).

## Problem statement

The soak evidence on MS-0MVLINY2Q004V33L shows the gate passes 20/20 quiet
(peak load 15.3), passes 2/2 at 8 burners (peak 23.6), and fails exactly one
wait — `turn to advance after end-of-turn presentation` — at load ≥ ≈31
(≈2× oversubscription, 16 burners, peak 32.8). That wait's budget is already at
the ceiling the 60 s hook permits, so no poll-budget tweak inside the hook can
rescue it.

Root cause (mechanism, verified against the installed `phaser` source):
Phaser's `TimeStep` clamps the per-frame delta it feeds scenes — under
`smoothStep` (default on) each frame contributes at most `1000/fps.min`
(200 ms) — and `Clock.elapsed`, which drives `delayedCall` timers and tween
progress, advances by that clamped delta. Under starvation (a few frames per
second) all game-time-paced choreography stretches: income phase gaps, coin
flights, the incident hold, and the deferral's own 250 ms `delayedCall`
re-polls. The deferral *deadline* (`s.time.now + INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS`,
where `s.time.now` is the raw frame timestamp) is wall-clock, but it is only
re-checked at those clamped polls, so the forced day start is delayed by the
same starvation. Aggregate: closing choreography (stretched) + 16 s cap
(late-detected) + boot > the 40 s budget and the 60 s hook.

The cap's stated purpose is "end-of-turn can never hang the game"
(CG-0MTR72P14000VO6Q, AC5/AC7). A stall bound that is only observed at frame
boundaries does not provide that guarantee — which is what this item fixes,
without touching the user-visible pacing.

## Users

- **Agent-implementer / gate runner** on the shared dev host: needs the browser
  gate green; a red `MainStreetScene` suite at ≈2× oversubscription burns whole
  sessions on retries and blocks the build → test → commit order.
- **Maintainer triaging a red browser suite**: needs a red wait to mean a
  behavioural regression, not host weather.
- **Release engineer** on the dev-push gate: a red gate on a loaded shared host
  stalls shipping even when the scene is correct.
- **Players**: unchanged pacing — the choreography, the incident hold and the
  cap value all stay as shipped; only the cap's *enforcement* becomes
  wall-clock rather than frame-clock, so under starvation the day advances at
  the documented bound instead of stalling past it.

Example user stories:

> As an agent running the browser gate on the shared 16-core host, I want the
> Enter-to-end-turn wait to pass at any load the host actually reaches, so that
> my gate result does not depend on which sibling suites happen to be running.

> As a player whose machine is momentarily overloaded, I want the end-of-turn
> to still advance within the documented safety window, so that the game can
> never appear hung.

## Existing state

- Measured envelope (2026-10-24, 16-core shared host): quiet 20/20 pass
  (peak 15.3); 8 burners 2/2 pass, then one fail at ambient 31.3; 16 burners
  fail at the 40 000 ms end-of-turn budget. Every other wait in the file passes
  at that load.
- The wait's effective budget is `capMs: INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` (16 000) +
  `floorMs: END_TURN_STARVATION_MARGIN_MS` (24 000) = 40 000 ms, the largest
  that keeps the documented 20 000 ms scene-boot allowance inside the 60 s
  `testTimeout` (asserted by `tests/tooling/wait-budget-guard.test.ts`). The
  suite's per-test timeout is already `it(..., 60_000)`.
- Five deferral polls race the choreography, all with the same shape
  (`startAt = <scene clock> + cap`, then `delayedCall(250, poll)`):
  3 in `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` (`advanceTurn` ~433,
  forced event-choice ~617, piggyback ~783) and 2 in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerAnimation.ts` (`finish`'s income wait
  ~254 and the reveal gating ~301).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerAnimation.ts` already has the
  degradation precedent: `scheduleOrRun` runs the callback immediately when the
  scene has no clock (headless), which a wall-clock helper must preserve.
- Node unit suites drive these polls through fake `time` stubs
  (`tests/main-street/competitive-closing-presentation.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/turnflow.test.ts`), and
  `tests/main-street/income-collection-cap.test.ts` pins "exactly three
  `s.time.now + INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` sites" by regex — both must be
  updated by the extraction.
- Reduced motion clears `incomeCollectionActive` synchronously in
  `MainStreetAnimatorIncome` (~line 1039), but it is **not** the remedy chosen:
  the parent rejected it as the sole remedy because it removes the
  deferred-income path from coverage.

## Desired change (decision: option C)

Replace the five duplicated deferral polls with **one shared, injectable
helper** that:

1. computes its deadline from a wall-clock timestamp (`Date.now()`),
2. re-polls with a wall-clock timer (`window.setTimeout`), not the scene clock,
3. forces completion (clearing `incomeCollectionActive` and invoking the
   caller's continuation) once `INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` of wall time has
   elapsed since the deferral began,
4. is enforced even when the page is not painting — a backgrounded/hidden
   document ahead of the cap forces the advance rather than waiting for the
   next animation frame (Q2 = 1), and
5. degrades to today's behaviour where no clock/timer exists (headless node
   scenes run the continuation immediately), and exposes its clock/timer for
   deterministic unit driving.

Options considered and rejected (recorded for traceability):

- **A — accept and document the envelope** (no code change): the gate can still
  go red on the shared host when ambient load spikes ≥2×, conflicting with the
  "red tree never pushed" policy; rejected in favour of a root-cause fix.
- **B — reduced-motion Enter test + a separate cheap deferral-contract test**:
  no production change, but downgrades the file's end-to-end end-of-turn test
  to a synthetic and couples coverage to a reduced-motion implementation
  detail; retained only as a fallback if C's soak does not pass.
- **D — raise the browser hook for this test**: pure masking, requires
  amending the parent's "any derived budget must leave headroom for boot plus
  teardown within that hook" AC and re-baselining the guard's headroom rule,
  and would fail again at ≈4× oversubscription; rejected.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **One bounded-deferral helper, wall-clock enforced.** All five
      income-collection deferral polls route through a single shared helper
      whose deadline is wall clock and whose re-poll is a wall timer; no inline
      `s.time.delayedCall(250, <poll>)` / `<scene clock> + INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS`
      poll remains. A unit test with a frozen scene clock and an advancing wall
      clock proves the continuation is forced within one poll interval of the
      16 000 ms cap.
- [ ] **Forced advance is not tied to paint.** When the document is hidden / no
      frame runs, the cap still forces the advance after the cap elapses
      (Q2 = 1). A unit test asserts the wall timer — not the scene clock —
      drives the assertion, and the behaviour is documented in the module's
      code comment.
- [ ] **Injectable and backward-compatible.** The helper accepts an injectable
      clock/timer (so `competitive-closing-presentation.test.ts`,
      `turnflow.test.ts` and the new tests drive it deterministically) and
      preserves today's no-clock degradation (headless scenes run the
      continuation immediately).
- [ ] **Single source of truth for the cap.** `INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` stays
      16 000 and remains the only cap value; the
      `tests/main-street/income-collection-cap.test.ts` "exactly three
      `s.time.now + INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` sites" pin is updated to the
      helper extraction (asserting the helper consumes the constant), so the
      duplication cannot silently return.
- [ ] **No production pacing change.** The choreography timing constants
      (`INCOME_PHASE_GAP_MS`, flight/stagger durations, `INCIDENT_REVEAL_HOLD_MS`)
      and the cap value are unchanged — pinned by existing/added unit tests;
      only the cap's enforcement mechanism differs.
- [ ] **Wait-budget guard still green.** `tests/tooling/wait-budget-guard.test.ts`
      passes unchanged: the end-of-turn wait keeps its cap-derived 40 000 ms
      budget and `budget + 20 s boot ≤ 60 s` headroom rule. If the soak shows
      the budget can now be reduced, that reduction is a *derived* margin
      change proved by the soak, not a hand-picked literal.
- [ ] **Reliability proven, not assumed.** `/skill:test --type soak-load`
      (≥ `nproc` burners) passes with the change, and the pre-change failure at
      the same burner count is reproduced and recorded on this item; both
      before/after tables (burners, peak load, runs, wall times, summary paths)
      are posted as a comment.
- [ ] **Documentation updated.** `docs/dev/testing.md` "Measured envelope" and
      the headroom rule section record the decision (cap enforced on wall
      clock, hidden-tab semantics) and the post-fix envelope, replacing the
      "above ~2× is outside the envelope" caveat with measured evidence; the
      helper's module comment documents the wall-clock contract. All related
      documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments,
      README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes
      (`/skill:test --type full`), evidence recorded on this item.

## Constraints

- **No behavioural change to production pacing.** The choreography, the
  incident hold and the cap value are shipped features
  (CG-0MT23O6W8003AXWJ, CG-0MTR72P14000VO6Q); only the cap's enforcement may
  change.
- The parent's headroom constraint stands: `budget + scene-boot allowance` must
  stay inside the browser 60 s hook.
- Reduced motion must not become the sole remedy (parent decision); the
  deferred-income path keeps explicit coverage.
- All five deferral sites must keep identical semantics after extraction, and
  the existing fake-clock unit suites must not be weakened to accommodate the
  change.
- A stale wall timer must never fire into a destroyed scene — reuse the
  existing `scene.isActive()` / try-catch defensive pattern from the deferred
  closing tail.
- Agent-initiated test runs go through the test skill only
  (`/skill:test --type soak-load`, `--type full`); no ad-hoc `npx vitest` loops.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerAnimation.ts` — add the shared
  wall-clock deferral helper (sibling to `scheduleOrRun` ~line 176); adopt it in
  `finish`'s income wait (~254) and the reveal gating (~301).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — three deferral sites
  (`advanceTurn` ~433, forced event-choice ~617, piggyback ~783) adopt the
  helper.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorTiming.ts` — `INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS`
  unchanged; comment updated to state the wall-clock enforcement contract.
- `tests/main-street/income-collection-cap.test.ts` — the "exactly three
  `s.time.now + cap` sites" regex pin moves to the helper extraction.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-closing-presentation.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/turnflow.test.ts` — fake `time` stubs: drive the injected
  timer/clock.
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts` — Enter test and its
  40 000 ms margin expected unchanged.
- `tests/tooling/wait-budget-guard.test.ts` — headroom rule re-check (expected
  unchanged).
- `docs/dev/testing.md` — "Measured envelope" + headroom rule: record the
  decision and the post-fix soak evidence.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the clamped-delta mechanism is the dominant starvation link
  and the deferral's poll cadence is the part that can be fixed without touching
  pacing. Verified against the installed Phaser source
  (`TimeStep.smoothDelta`, `Clock.now` / `Clock.elapsed` semantics); the
  before/after `soak-load` run is the confirmation.
- **Risk:** removing the late-detection link may not be sufficient on its own —
  the choreography phases before/after the deferral still stretch under
  clamped delta. Mitigation: the soak is a hard AC; if it still fails, the
  fallback is option B's separate deferral-contract test (not option D), and
  the residual envelope is re-documented with evidence.
- **Risk (accepted, decided):** a wall-clock cap changes hidden/backgrounded-tab
  behaviour — the day start is now forced after the cap instead of stalling
  until the tab paints again (Q2 = 1). This is the intended semantics of a stall
  bound; documented in the module comment and `docs/dev/testing.md`.
- **Risk:** a wall timer outliving the scene could fire into a destroyed scene.
  Mitigation: `scene.isActive()` guard plus the existing try-catch pattern; a
  unit test covers the destroyed/stale case.
- **Risk (scope creep):** the attractor is "rework all game-time animation off
  clamped delta" (tweens, phase gaps, incident hold). Explicitly out of scope —
  record as linked work items rather than expanding this one.

## Related work

- MS-0MVMKEU2000639TG — this item (`discovered-from:` the soak child
  MS-0MVLINY2Q004V33L; soak evidence and envelope recorded there and in
  `docs/dev/testing.md` "Measured envelope").
- MS-0MVK2ACLN004VVIJ — parent: made the file's waits load-tolerant via
  cap-derived budgets; its headroom AC and "Measured limit (triaged, not a
  flake)" section are the origin of this item.
- MS-0MVLINY2Q004V33L — the 20-run / under-load soak whose evidence defines the
  envelope and whose `soak-load` profile proves this fix.
- MS-0MVLINWV10005H2P — the wait-budget guard and headroom rule this item must
  keep green.
- MS-0MUYFX7Q2004JQ5R — shared end-of-turn closing presentation primitive that
  carries `incomeCollectionCapMs`.
- CG-0MT23O6W8003AXWJ / CG-0MTR72P14000VO6Q — phased income choreography and
  deferred income window (untouched pacing; the property the cap protects).
- MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41 (open) — planned End-of-Turn summary dialog on the
  closing completion path; it will interact with the deferral this item
  extracts, so check dependency direction during planning.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MVLINY2Q004V33L** – Prove browser-wait reliability: 20-run soak plus under-load run (completed)
- **MS-0MVLINWV10005H2P** – Guard browser wait budgets against production caps (completed)
- **MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41** – End of Turn summary… (open; planned dialog on the closing path)

### Related repository files
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — engine developer guide; frame-loop/delta context.
- `docs/dev/testing.md` — measured envelope and headroom rule this item updates.
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — documents reduced motion, deferral pacing and
  presentation behaviour these waits must respect.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Given the measured envelope (the gate fails only above ≈2× CPU
  oversubscription, load ≥ ~31), which remediation should this item
  implement — (A) accept and document the envelope with no code change,
  (B) convert the Enter test to reduced motion plus a separate cheap
  deferral-contract test, (C) make the income-collection deferral cap
  starvation-proof (wall-clock deadline + wall-clock poll, one extracted
  helper, production change confined to the safety cap), or (D) raise the
  browser hook for this test (parent AC amendment needed)?"
  — Answer (producer): **C** — make the income-collection deferral cap
  starvation-proof. Source: interactive reply (intake interview round 1,
  2026-10-25). Agent recommendation was C (stated with rationale before the
  answer); A was recorded as the zero-production-change fallback and B's second
  variant as the fallback if C's soak still fails. Research behind the
  recommendation: Phaser `TimeStep.smoothDelta` clamps per-frame delta to
  `1000/fps.min` (200 ms default), so under rAF starvation the choreography and
  the deferral's 250 ms `delayedCall` re-polls both run at a fraction of
  wall-clock speed — the wall-clock cap deadline is therefore detected late,
  which is the link C removes.
- Q2 (conditional on C): "Should the 16 000 ms cap be enforced against wall
  clock even when the page is not painting/visible (backgrounded tab or fully
  starved rAF — the day start is forced after 16 s wall even though the
  choreography never ran), or should the forced advance hold while the document
  is hidden/blurred and resume on visibility change?"
  — Answer (producer): **as recommended** = enforce on wall clock (option 1):
  the cap is a stall bound, nothing is visible while hidden, and today a hidden
  tab already stalls the animator indefinitely. Source: interactive reply
  (intake interview round 1, 2026-10-25). Recorded as an accepted, documented
  semantic change in the Risks section and to be reflected in the helper's
  module comment and `docs/dev/testing.md`.
data.title: Enter-to-end-turn browser wait exceeds the 60 s hook above ~2x CPU oversubscription

# Bailout overlay UI and deferred closing resume

Parent: MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG (Bank Loans). Depends on the single-player bailout slice.

## Goal

When a bailout offer is open, the player sees a dialog listing the loan options with their
per-turn and total repayment plus a Decline button, and accepting or declining resumes the
turn exactly once.

## Context

- Overlay conventions: `createOverlayBackground` / `createOverlayButton` from `@ui`, all
  elements parented into `s.hudContainer`, depths 199/200/201, every object pushed into
  `s.overlayObjects`, `safePlaySound` for SFX, reduced-motion safe instant appearance.
- Precedents: `showEventChoiceDialog` / `showPiggybackDialog` /
  `showTurnSummaryDialog` in `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts`, delegated from
  `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts`; pure Phaser-free models such as
  `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts` (`MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` is the newest
  example) keep the content testable without a browser.
- Resume path: the deferred closing tail is re-run from
  `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` (`finishTurnPresentation` /
  `finishDeferredTurnClosing`) — the same shape used for pending event choices.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts` must not present game-over while a bailout
  offer is open, but must present the normal bankruptcy summary after a decline.
- The Turn Summary "Bank Loan" button (`onBankLoanAction` seam in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` / `MainStreetScene.ts`) is deliberately a
  separate follow-up item — do not wire it here.

## Desired change

1. New pure model `src/scenes/MainStreetLoanOverlayModel.ts` (or equivalent) building the
   option rows from `pendingLoanOffer` + `config.loanOptions`: principal, per-turn
   repayment, total repayment, term.
2. New `src/scenes/MainStreetLoanOverlay.ts` rendering the dialog with one button per
   option and a Decline button, following the overlay conventions above.
3. Wire presentation into the turn controller: when `result.pendingLoanOffer` is set, show
   the overlay instead of the game-over summary; on resolution call the loan accept/decline
   handler and then run the deferred closing tail exactly once.
4. Tests: model test for the option rows, overlay browser test for render + button count +
   dismiss behaviour, and a turn-flow test proving the closing resumes once (no replay, no
   duplicate offer).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A bailout overlay is rendered whenever a pending loan offer exists, listing each loan option with its per-turn and total repayment plus a Decline choice.
- Accepting or declining the offer resumes the deferred closing sequence, and the game-over summary is not shown while a bailout offer is open.
- Tests assert the overlay is presented once per offer, the resume completes the closing exactly once, and no replay or duplicate-offer loop occurs.

## Key Files:

- `src/scenes/MainStreetLoanOverlay.ts` — new overlay dialog
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — dialog presentation following the event-choice pattern
- `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — delegation method
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — deferred-closing resume wiring
- `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts` — suppress game-over while an offer is open
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetLoanOverlay.test.ts` — new model/flow tests
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetLoanOverlay.browser.test.ts` — new overlay browser test
data.title: Bailout overlay UI and deferred closing resume

# Intake brief: Host memory pressure kills long-lived dev servers mid-session (swap exhaustion)

**Type:** chore · **Priority:** medium · **Cross-repo:** no (host action + tooling + docs) · **Discovered-from:** MS-0MVREB31W004F48D

**Producer decisions (2026-10-29):** Q1 = b (docs/runbook + committed read-only `scripts/hygiene_check.sh`); Q2 = a (prune only confirmed-orphaned, clean, unregistered worktree dirs after listing; no process kills); Q3 = a (documented concurrency guideline + pre-start checks, no enforcement).

## Problem statement

Long-lived `vite --host` dev servers on this development host are dying mid-session, leaving the browser with `[vite] server connection lost`, failed HMR WebSocket retries and `net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED` for every card SVG / `csv-checksum.json` request. The host is under sustained memory pressure (swap essentially full) with many orphaned worktree checkouts and concurrent sibling workloads, but the exact kill mechanism is not yet confirmed. This item owns the **host-level remediation** that the diagnosis in `docs/dev/testing.md` explicitly defers to it.

## Users

- **Developers and agents running long-lived dev sessions** — need a `npm run dev` session to survive a working session so they can exercise the UI and HMR loop.
  - *User story:* "As a developer, I want my `vite --host` dev server to stay up for the duration of a session, so a mid-session asset flood does not force me to restart and lose my place."
- **Producer / on-call operator** — needs a safe, repeatable way to reclaim host memory (stale worktrees, orphaned servers) without risking uncommitted work.
  - *User story:* "As the operator, I want a documented, approval-gated hygiene procedure so I can reduce host pressure without deleting someone's in-progress work."
- **Agents running implement/test workflows** — depend on a stable dev server and watch budget on the host.
  - *User story:* "As an agent, I want concurrent `vite --host` servers capped and stale checkouts pruned so my test and dev runs are not starved or killed."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Root-cause determination documented.** A findings section records, for each candidate cause, whether it is confirmed, ruled out, or undetermined, citing the commands and evidence used:
   - (a) kernel / `systemd-oomd` OOM kill of the `vite`/`node` process;
   - (b) manual or agent kill (including `wl cleanup-worktree`, which `implement.py finish`/`abort` invokes, and terminal/session termination);
   - (c) `:3000` port conflict (structurally a startup failure, not a mid-session kill).
   *Verification:* the finding is present in the work-item/docs and each hypothesis is explicitly resolved or marked undetermined with rationale.

2. **Safe worktree-hygiene procedure, committed helper, and evidenced execution (Q1 = b, Q2 = a).** A committed, read-only `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` reports registered worktrees vs orphaned directories under `.worklog/worktrees`, swap/memory pressure, and orphaned dev servers; it never prunes or kills. A documented procedure distinguishes registered git worktrees (`git worktree list`) from orphaned directories, lists candidates for approval, and prunes **only** confirmed-orphaned, clean, unregistered directories — never `--force`, never registered worktrees, never stashes. Per Q2 (option a) the procedure is executed on this host and before/after counts are recorded (intake snapshot: **31 directories vs 15 registered worktrees including main → ~16 orphaned/unregistered**).
   *Verification:* the script runs on this host and reports the expected inventory; a test covers its detection logic; the procedure is present in docs and before/after counts are recorded as evidence.

3. **Dev-server concurrency cap and restart/swap-reclamation procedure documented (Q3 = a).** The existing `docs/dev/testing.md` troubleshooting section is extended with: pre-start checks (`free -m`, `swapon --show`, `ss -ltn | grep :3000`, process count), a documented cap on simultaneous `vite --host` servers across checkouts, and a step-by-step restart plus swap-reclamation procedure.
   *Verification:* the docs section exists and is cross-referenced from the README dev-server section.

4. **Post-remediation validation.** After the approved cleanup, record `free -m` / `swapon --show` before and after and confirm swap headroom improves, and confirm a dev session survives a documented soak (e.g. ≥30 min `npm run dev` with the card asset tree loaded) with no connection-lost cascade.
   *Verification:* before/after metrics plus the soak observation are recorded.

5. **Documentation and suite.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries. The full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Environmental scope:** host actions, read-only tooling (`scripts/hygiene_check.sh`) and documentation; no product runtime behaviour change. `CHANGELOG.md` is excluded (managed by the ship pipeline).
- **Destructive actions require explicit producer/operator approval:** removing worktree directories, killing processes, or deleting stashes. Never `git worktree prune --force`; never remove a registered worktree or a stash without triage.
- **Worktree isolation:** any committed change is made via the implement skill's worktree; `wl` and host commands run from the main checkout.
- **No ad-hoc test runs:** every agent-initiated test run goes through the test skill.
- **Ignore rules:** `.worklog/*` is gitignored, so host evidence belongs in work-item comments, not committed files.

## Existing state

- **Memory:** swap **8187 / 8191 MB used (100 %)**; RAM 30 GB with ~12 GB available at intake time (`free -m`, `swapon --show`).
- **Worktrees:** 31 directories under `.worklog/worktrees`; `git worktree list` reports 15 worktrees including main (14 under `.worklog`) → ~16 orphaned/unregistered directories. Some are empty stubs (dated 7–10 Oct); others are full stale checkouts.
- **Concurrent sibling workloads observed:** `AI_Hell` vitest unit/integration plus a `vite preview --port 4173` (4 h+), `tce-the-rising` vitest browser (11 min), and many `ContextHub` `tsx` node processes (7 h+).
- **OOM evidence:** `systemd-oomd` active since 2026-10-18; **no kernel/oomd OOM-kill records on the current boot (18 Oct → now)**. The 729 OOM log lines all belong to the previous boot (2026-10-03: vitest workers, esbuild, dbus, systemd). So swap exhaustion at report time did **not** produce a kernel OOM kill on this boot.
- **Port:** no listener on `:3000` now — consistent with a dead server, not a bound/conflicting port. A mid-session port conflict is structurally implausible (Vite binds at startup).
- **Process tracking:** `wl cleanup-worktree` SIGTERMs tracked worktree-scoped processes; main-checkout dev servers are not tracked, and **0 processes were tracked** at intake.
- **Docs:** `docs/dev/testing.md` already diagnoses the cascade ("Troubleshooting: dev server died mid-session") and explicitly defers host remediation to this item.
- **Gap (in scope, Q1 = b):** the global AGENTS.md workflow-hygiene rule references `scripts/hygiene_check.sh`, which **does not exist** in this repo; this item adds it as a read-only detector.
- **Existing tooling:** the read-only `machine-hygiene` skill proposes kill/renice/prune actions but has no worktree pruning; the `cleanup` skill prunes branches, not worktrees.

## Desired change

1. A documented, evidence-backed root-cause determination (confirm or bound the kill cause).
2. Reduced host pressure: approval-gated pruning of orphaned worktrees, a committed read-only `scripts/hygiene_check.sh`, a documented concurrent-dev-server cap, and a restart/swap-reclamation runbook.
3. Recorded before/after host state so the improvement is verifiable.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/dev/testing.md` — primary: extend the existing "dev server died mid-session" section into a host-pressure / worktree-hygiene runbook.
- `README.md` — cross-reference the restart procedure from the dev-server section (~line 220).
- `AGENTS.md` (repo) — optional cross-reference to the hygiene procedure.
- `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` — new read-only detector (worktree inventory, swap/memory pressure, orphaned dev servers); referenced by AGENTS.md but currently absent. Must include a focused test.

## Related work

- **MS-0MVREB31W004F48D** — Dev-session browser console errors: `/api/transcripts` 404 and dev-server drop cascade (completed). Source item; established the diagnosis and deferred host remediation here.
- **MS-0MV8M9IAF000KPNY** — Host inotify watcher exhaustion (ENOSPC) breaks main-checkout test runs (completed). Sibling host-pressure item; precedent for a diagnosis-plus-remediation chore.
- **MS-0MVBEQ6MC004WRI0** / **MS-0MVSXXSMV003XKGI** — Vite watcher-ignore ports across sibling game repos. Adjacent watcher/worktree pressure work; explicitly out of scope here.
- **Skills:** `machine-hygiene` (read-only pressure analysis + approved remediation), `cleanup` (branch pruning), `test` (gated suite runs).
- **Docs:** `docs/dev/testing.md` (§ dev-server troubleshooting, § ENOSPC), `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md`.

## Risks, assumptions, and failure modes

- **Data-loss risk:** pruning a worktree that holds uncommitted work. *Mitigation:* approval-gated, clean-only, registered-vs-orphaned check, `git status` per candidate, never `--force`.
- **Disruption risk:** killing a legitimately active dev server or test run. *Mitigation:* ancestry/age check and owner confirmation before any kill.
- **Scope-creep risk:** expanding into the watcher-ignore port family (MS-0MVBEQ6MC004WRI0). *Mitigation:* record any extra opportunities as linked work items, not scope.
- **Undetermined-cause risk:** the exact kill may be unrecoverable from available logs. *Mitigation:* AC1 requires "confirmed **or bounded**", not "prove OOM".
- **Assumption:** the affected dev server ran from the main checkout, so `wl cleanup-worktree` did not kill it. *Verify during implementation.*
- **Assumption:** log retention on the current boot covers the report window (verified: 18–29 Oct present).
- **Decision (Q3 = a):** "cap concurrent dev servers" is a documented guideline plus pre-start checks, not a new enforcement mechanism; no launcher/registry is added.
- **Tooling risk:** a new shell script without tests. *Mitigation:* keep it read-only and add a focused test for the inventory/classification logic.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

The seed context plus repo/host research was sufficient to draft the initial brief, so no interactive round was held before drafting. The three decisions below were routed to the producer and answered on 2026-10-29.

- **Q1 — Delivery form for the guardrails?** Options: (a) docs/runbook only; (b) docs/runbook + a small committed `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` that reports stale worktrees, swap pressure, orphaned dev servers; (c) docs + a dev-server launcher wrapper.
  **Answer (producer):** **(b)** — docs/runbook plus a committed read-only `scripts/hygiene_check.sh`. Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-29.
  **Recommended at draft time: (b)** — the global AGENTS.md already references `scripts/hygiene_check.sh`, and a repeatable check is the durable fix.
  *Research:* file absent from repo; `machine-hygiene` covers process-level pressure but not worktree inventory.

- **Q2 — Approval to perform destructive host cleanup now?** Options: (a) prune only confirmed-orphaned, clean, unregistered directories after listing them; (b) also kill orphaned/abandoned dev servers; (c) detection only, defer all cleanup.
  **Answer (producer):** **(a)** — prune only confirmed-orphaned, clean, unregistered directories after listing them; no process kills. Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-29.
  **Recommended at draft time: (a)**, then re-assess for (b) with an explicit list.

- **Q3 — Does "cap concurrent dev servers" need technical enforcement or a documented guideline?** Options: (a) documented guideline + pre-start checks; (b) a launcher/registry that refuses a second server; (c) no cap, restart procedure only.
  **Answer (producer):** **(a)** — documented guideline plus pre-start checks; no enforcement mechanism. Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-29.
  **Recommended at draft time: (a)** — keeps the item environmental and non-speculative.

### Research performed

- Reviewed the current boot's kernel/oomd logs (`journalctl -b -g 'Out of memory|oom-kill|Killed process'`, `journalctl -u systemd-oomd`): no OOM kills since 2026-10-18; the 729 historical OOM lines are from the 2026-10-03 boot.
- Inventoried worktrees (`git worktree list` vs `.worklog/worktrees` directory count): 15 registered vs 31 directories.
- Inventoried live processes: sibling vitest/vite preview/serve and ContextHub node processes consuming memory.
- Read `docs/dev/testing.md` §§ dev-server troubleshooting / ENOSPC; confirmed this item is the deferred host-remediation follow-up.
- Inspected `wl cleanup-worktree` and `implement.py` `cleanup_worktree_processes` to characterise the agent-kill hypothesis.
- Ran the find-related skill (automated report merged above).

# tce-main-street dev builds re-pin the engine when it advances, invalidating the test cache and pushing the full suite past `timeoutPerCommand`

**Headline:** When the engine `dev` tip has advanced past the pinned SHA, `npm run build` re-pins the engine and stages `configs/engine-pin.json` + the `core` gitlink, so the finish gate re-runs the full suite against a *dirty* tree that can exceed `timeoutPerCommand` on a loaded host. Producer decisions are recorded: this repo owns the immediate unblock (timeout + guard + docs); the finish-gate composition exclusion and the vitest/`suiteCommands` changed-scope fixes land in **SorraAgents** and are cross-referenced here.

## Problem statement

`implement.py finish` runs **build → test → commit** in a worktree. The build runs `npm run build`, whose first step is `npm run engine:sync`. When the engine's tracked branch tip has advanced beyond a worktree's committed pin, `engine:sync` runs `git submodule update --remote core`, rewrites `configs/engine-pin.json` and **stages the pin and the `core` gitlink** (`core/scripts/engine-sync.mjs`, `stageEngineState`). The test gate then evaluates a tree that is dirty *because of the build*, and the cache key (`skill/test_cache.py:compute_git_state` — `HEAD` plus the content of every dirty path) no longer matches any pre-warmed green entry. On the shared host the resulting full-suite run measured **2846 s**, above `timeoutPerCommand: 1800`, and the gate failed with `Test run 1/3 failed (unknown)`, `failures: []` — a kill/unparsed failure presented as a code failure.

Two independent defects compound it:

1. **`changed-scope` is silently disabled for this repo.** `changed_scope_commands()` returns `None` immediately when `.pi/test-config.json` declares `suiteCommands` (the documented fast path is unavailable here), and even without that guard `map_changed_to_tests()` only understands pytest and `*.test.mjs` node tests — it has no vitest/`.test.ts` mapping. `implement.py finish` therefore warns `changed-scope selection unavailable … falling back to full scope` and every finish, including docs/evidence-only items, pays the full suite (reproduced twice; `/tmp/ms0mvpy2-finish.log` line 4).
2. **Queue time is indistinguishable from test time, and a kill is indistinguishable from a failure.** The host-wide test semaphore (`TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY=2`) is shared by all repos; measured slot waits of 1040–2400 s appeared as `slot_busy`, and a non-zero/killed run with no parsable failures reported `reason: unknown`. `timeoutPerCommand` bounds the whole command, and the documented remediation ("set it high enough to cover the full suite with headroom") is currently 1800 against a measured 2846 s.

## Producer decisions (resolved)

All three decisions were made by the producer in-session (source: interactive reply `A / A / A`, recorded in the Appendix). They fix the scope and design:

- **Q1 = A — scope and home.** This MS item owns the requirements, evidence and the **repo-local** `.pi/test-config.json` timeout/docs mitigation. The framework behaviour fixes are filed in **SorraAgents** and cross-referenced here (precedent: `MS-0MVN0G6VB000ZF57` → `SA-0MVO274QN006GXGQ`). This item is **not** an epic and remains a `bug`; the SA items are tracked in SorraAgents and cross-referenced here.
- **Q2 = A — engine re-pin remedy.** The finish gate must not commit or test build-artefact churn it did not originate: exclude the `core` gitlink and `configs/engine-pin.json` from the finish commit unless the item itself changed the engine composition, and prove that the tested composition equals the committed composition. Do **not** relax the cache key (remedy B rejected) and do **not** change `engine:sync` to verify-only (remedy C rejected).
- **Q3 = A — changed-scope approach.** Add a vitest/TS-aware selection and honour declared `groups` even when `suiteCommands` is present. `suiteCommands` defines the **full** suite only; it must no longer disable selection.

## Users

- **Implement agent (primary) — user story:** "As an implement agent finishing a work item, I need the finish gate to test the engine composition that will actually be committed, and to reuse a valid green cache entry, so a documentation- or evidence-only item is not blocked by a 47-minute unrelated engine suite."
- **Implement agent — user story:** "When the gate fails, I need to know whether it was a code failure, a suite timeout, or a test-slot wait, so I fix the right thing instead of retrying blindly."
- **Repo maintainer — user story:** "As the maintainer, I want an engine bump to be a deliberate, reviewable change, not a side effect silently swept into every documentation commit."
- **Release operator — user story:** "I need the pin and the `core` gitlink to remain coherent, so the release pin-contract gate stays trustworthy."

## Acceptance Criteria

Each AC names the repo that owns it. AC1–AC3 are satisfied by the cross-referenced SorraAgents items; AC4–AC5 land here.

- [ ] **AC1 — no build-artefact churn in the tested/committed tree (SorraAgents, Q2=A).** With a worktree created from a commit whose `configs/engine-pin.json` lags the engine tracked tip, `implement.py finish` on a source-unchanged item does **not** let `npm run build`'s `engine:sync` re-pin or gitlink advance become part of the item's commit. The tested composition equals the committed composition (the pin in `HEAD`), and the gate verdict records the composed engine SHA plus whether the suite ran or was cache-served. The test cache key is unchanged (remedy B rejected). Proven by a git-fixture test with a submodule whose checkout HEAD differs from the recorded gitlink, plus a live run on this repo.
- [ ] **AC2 — `changed-scope` works for this repo (SorraAgents, Q3=A).** For a change set covered by a declared `groups` entry or by a changed vitest test file, `implement.py finish` runs the targeted selection and reports `scope: changed` with the selected commands; declaring `suiteCommands` no longer disables selection, and `suiteCommands` continues to define only the full suite. When no safe subset exists, the fallback names the specific reason (e.g. "no changed source/test files", "no matching group") instead of a generic list. Proven by selector unit tests (vitest/TS + `suiteCommands` + groups) and a live finish log showing `scope: changed`.
- [ ] **AC3 — timeout and queue failures are self-describing (SorraAgents, coordinated with `SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI`).** A suite that exceeds `timeoutPerCommand`, or is killed without parsable failures, is reported as an infrastructure/timeout condition (never `reason: unknown` with `failures: []`), including the configured timeout, elapsed time, and — separately — the semaphore queue wait. Queue wait is not charged to the suite's per-command timeout, or is reported as its own `slot_busy` duration. Proven by gate-classification unit tests and a simulated timeout/kill fixture.
- [ ] **AC4 — honest, bounded timeout configuration and documentation (this repo).** `timeoutPerCommand` is set from measured evidence to cover the loaded-host full suite with headroom (measured 2846 s → set 3600 s; confirm whether it is per command or per suite first), and a guard test fails if it is lowered below the documented measured worst case plus headroom. `docs/dev/testing.md` and `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` record the measured values, the per-command/queue semantics, the engine composition at finish, and the remediation; framework docs (`implement/SKILL.md`, the test skill reference) are updated where the SA behaviour changes.
- [ ] **AC5 — validation and full suite.** Reproduced and pinned by a test at each module under change; all related documentation is updated (including code comments and README where relevant); the full project test suite passes with the new changes (framework node/pytest suites for SorraAgents changes; this repo's suite for repo-local changes).

## Constraints

- **Pin policy is preserved.** `CG-0MVO268500071BPI` requires the pin to track the engine `dev` tip and the pin + gitlink to travel together in one commit. Q2=A does not stop `engine:sync` from running on dev builds; it only prevents the **finish gate** from sweeping that build-originated churn into an item's commit. Any further deviation needs producer sign-off.
- **Repository boundaries.** This repo must not edit `.pi/` or the agent framework in `~/.pi/agent/skills` directly; framework fixes land in **SorraAgents** and are cross-referenced (Q1=A). The engine-sync script remains canonical in **Tableau-Card-Engine** and is **not** changed (Q2 ≠ C).
- **Cache correctness over speed.** The cache key is not relaxed (Q2 ≠ B); a green entry recorded on a different engine must never satisfy the gate (see `SA-0MVCTZRZD004CE3L`).
- **Test execution policy.** Validation runs go through `/skill:test`; no ad-hoc suites. The host test semaphore must not be bypassed.
- **`timeoutPerCommand` is shared.** `implement.py` also uses it as the `git push` timeout, so raising it widens the push window too.
- **Language.** UK English throughout.

## Existing state

- `configs/engine-pin.json` and the `core` gitlink are currently coherent at `f5c0a1b1` (= local `core` HEAD = `origin/dev` tip), so the main checkout is clean; the failure requires a lagging pin (a worktree from an older commit or an engine advance after the worktree was created).
- Evidence (read-only, outside the repo):
  - `/tmp/ms0mvpy2-finish.log` — `engine:sync: core updated 0409c1eb5f → 19f30ac713`, pin staged; gate result `success: false`, `notices: []`, `reason: unknown`, `phase_finish` 2215 s.
  - `/tmp/ms0mvpy2-full.log` — green full suite, `elapsed: 2846.6 s`.
  - `/tmp/ms0mvpy2ydq-finish.log` — `reason: slot_contention`, slot wait 2400 s.
  - `/tmp/ms0mvpy2-warm3.log` — `slot_busy` after 1500 s.
- Current config: `.pi/test-config.json` `timeoutPerCommand: 1800`, `suiteCommands` = 3 commands (`npm --silent test`, MainStreetScene browser, e2e no-console-errors), plus 10 named `groups`.
- Existing guards: engine checkout preflight (`tests/tooling/engine-checkout-precheck.ts`, `MS-0MVO26G5H0054SNV`) fails loudly when `./core` is behind the pin; `tests/main-street/engine-submodule-sync.test.ts` holds the release pin contract.
- Framework facts: `changed_scope_commands()` early-returns on `suiteCommands`; `map_changed_to_tests()` supports `.py` / `*.test.mjs` only; `_run_cached_paced()` reports slot contention but the guarded path's `run_suite()` catches `TimeoutExpired` as `suite_timeout`; a non-zero/killed run with no parsable output becomes `GATE_FAILURE_UNKNOWN`.

## Desired change

1. **Repo-local unblock (this item, tce-main-street):** raise `timeoutPerCommand` from measured evidence with headroom (measured 2846 s → 3600 s), add a config guard test, and document the gate's composition/caching/timeout semantics.
2. **Framework fixes (SorraAgents, cross-referenced here):**
   - **SA-item A — finish-gate composition exclusion.** Exclude build-originated submodule gitlink/pin churn from the finish commit when the item did not change engine composition, prove tested composition = committed composition, and record the composed engine SHA + cache provenance in every verdict. Extends `SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2` / `SA-0MVQHVGFR006W8LG` rather than duplicating them.
   - **SA-item B — changed-scope for `suiteCommands` + vitest/TS.** Honour declared `groups` and add a vitest/TS selection; `suiteCommands` defines the full suite only. Builds on `SA-0MUJKF2HP001BR51`.
   - **SA-item C — timeout/queue classification.** Distinguish timeout/kill from unparsed failure, report timeout + elapsed + queue wait separately, and keep queue wait out of the per-command timeout. Coordinate with `SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI` (slot fairness) and `SA-0MUKHCO02009EQFG` (pacer).
3. **Engine repo (Tableau-Card-Engine):** no change — verify-only sync (remedy C) rejected.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.pi/test-config.json` — `timeoutPerCommand` value, `suiteCommands`, `groups`; add a guard test covering the measured worst case.
- `docs/dev/testing.md` — finish-gate composition, cache-key, timeout and queue-wait semantics.
- `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` — composition matrix; state what the finish gate composes and commits.
- `tests/tooling/engine-checkout-precheck.ts`, `tests/main-street/engine-submodule-sync.test.ts` — existing guards to extend/reuse for the lagging-pin fixture.
- `package.json` — `build` runs `engine:sync` first; the finish gate's build entry point.
- `configs/engine-pin.json` — the pin that must travel with the gitlink.
- `core/scripts/engine-sync.mjs` (canonical in Tableau-Card-Engine) — reference only; no change expected.
- SorraAgents (`~/.pi/agent/skills`): `test/scripts/run_tests.py` (`changed_scope_commands`, `map_changed_to_tests`, `select_group_from_changed_files`, `run_suite` timeout notices), `test_cache.py` (`compute_git_state`), `implement/scripts/implement.py` (`phase_finish`, `run_tests`, `_run_resolved_suite`, `_gate_failure_kind`, `git_commit`), `implement/SKILL.md`.

## Related work

- **MS-0MVMKEU2000639TG** — origin epic (Enter-to-end-turn browser wait under load); this item was discovered while finishing its evidence-only child.
- **MS-0MVO26G5H0054SNV** — engine checkout preflight (composed vs pinned engine); complementary loud-failure guard.
- **MS-0MVN1OAG1005JWFX** — pin-tracks-tip policy and mechanical re-pin; the policy Q2=A preserves.
- **MS-0MVN0G6VB000ZF57** — precedent: release derived-files step must never stage submodule pointer changes (fix landed in `SA-0MVO274QN006GXGQ`); the template for AC1 and for the MS → SA cross-reference pattern.
- **MS-0MVCRGKZY007DIED** — auto-sync engine on dev builds, pin release builds; the behaviour that creates the churn.
- **MS-0MVRAH7O9007L79A**, **MS-0MVOCF9T5007CH2A**, **MS-0MVOCF4E2004PEVZ** — pin verification and documentation precedents.
- **SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2** (open) — finish gate must test the tree the commit produces; **SA-0MVQHVGFR006W8LG** (blocked) — temp-index staging; both are the base for SA-item A.
- **SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI** (open, high) — slot fairness/starvation; **SA-0MVEEALZR0029DD7** — single-flight coalescing; **SA-0MVEDMM3N004Y6MO** — semaphore wait telemetry; together with **SA-0MUKHCO02009EQFG** (pacer) they own the queue side of SA-item C.
- **SA-0MVCTZRZD004CE3L** (open) — cache key ignores worktree/env identity; Q2=A leaves the key unchanged, so this remains the guard against false greens.
- **SA-0MUJKF2HP001BR51** — targeted test groups (avoid full-suite timeouts); the mechanism SA-item B builds on.
- **MS-0MVPY2X7L001DW7J**, **MS-0MVPY2YDQ000S0G6** — blocked children of the origin epic that paid this cost twice.

## Risks and assumptions

- **R1 — test/commit composition mismatch.** Q2=A excludes the build's engine advance from the commit, but the build has still advanced `./core` when the suite runs. The implementation must restore or pin the tested composition to the committed pin (e.g. restore the gitlink/pin after the build, or run the suite through the temp index) and record the composed engine SHA; otherwise a green run could describe a different engine than the commit. This is the primary design risk for SA-item A.
- **R2 — slide into remedy C.** If the only workable way to make tested composition equal committed composition is to stop `engine:sync` at finish, that is remedy C (rejected) and needs producer sign-off; do not drift into it silently.
- **R3 — longer worst-case gate.** Raising the timeout to 3600 s means a genuinely stuck suite occupies a host slot for an hour; with only 2 slots this can worsen starvation. Mitigation: land the queue-wait separation/fairness work alongside (SA-item C), and keep the retry count bounded.
- **R4 — scope creep.** Vitest-aware changed-scope selection may be a substantial framework feature. Mitigation: SA-item B is its own item; the `groups`-based path can land first if the selector is large.
- **A1 — reproducing the exact failure.** The current pin is coherent, so a deterministic repro needs a fixture with a lagging pin (or a controlled engine advance), not a live worktree today. AC1/AC3 should be proven with fixtures first and a live run second.
- **A2 — timeout granularity.** It is not yet confirmed whether `timeoutPerCommand` bounds each `suiteCommands` entry or the aggregated run; AC4's value depends on this. Confirm it during implementation.
- **A3 — cause of the 2215 s `unknown`.** The evidence (no notice, no parsable failures, only Phaser stderr) is consistent with a kill/OOM or a worker crash rather than a clean `TimeoutExpired`; AC3 requires correct classification regardless of cause, not a specific root cause.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1 — Where should the fix live and how much should this item own?**
  Options: (A) this MS item owns requirements + evidence + the repo-local timeout/docs mitigation, with framework fixes filed in SorraAgents and cross-referenced (precedent `MS-0MVN0G6VB000ZF57` → `SA-0MVO274QN006GXGQ`); (B) this MS item is an epic whose children span MS + SA + engine repos; (C) repo-local mitigation only; (D) move the whole item to SorraAgents.
  **Recommended:** A — keeps the repo-local unblock visible here while the framework fix lands where the code lives.
  **Answer (producer, in-session reply):** **A**. Source: interactive reply to the Q1–Q3 round on 2026-10-29; question recorded in comment `MS-C0MVT386C0000OU0X`. Supersedes the earlier "OPEN QUESTION" state.

- **Q2 — Which remedy should govern the engine re-pin / cache interaction (AC1)?**
  Options: (A) the finish gate must not commit/test build-artefact churn it did not originate — exclude the submodule gitlink + engine pin from the finish commit unless the item touched them, and test the committed composition; (B) exclude the engine gitlink/pin pair from the test-cache key; (C) make `engine:sync` a no-op (verify-only) at finish; (D) only raise `timeoutPerCommand`.
  **Recommended:** A — removes the silent unrelated engine bump and the cache mismatch without weakening the pin policy or the cache's correctness.
  **Answer (producer, in-session reply):** **A**. Source: interactive reply to the Q1–Q3 round on 2026-10-29; question recorded in comment `MS-C0MVT386C0000OU0X`. Supersedes the earlier "OPEN QUESTION" state.

- **Q3 — How should the changed-scope fast path be restored (AC2)?**
  Options: (A) add a vitest/TS-aware selection and honour declared `groups` even when `suiteCommands` is present (`suiteCommands` defines the full suite only); (B) rely on `groups` only, requiring every change to map to a declared group (add a catch-all); (C) remove `suiteCommands` from this repo and rely on convention detection; (D) skip changed-scope and only fix queue/timeout handling.
  **Recommended:** A — restores the documented fast path for this stack without weakening the full-suite gate.
  **Answer (producer, in-session reply):** **A**. Source: interactive reply to the Q1–Q3 round on 2026-10-29; question recorded in comment `MS-C0MVT386C0000OU0X`. Supersedes the earlier "OPEN QUESTION" state.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MVN1OAG1005JWFX** – Engine pin lags the core dev tip, so engine:verify throws PIN MISMATCH (completed)
- **MS-0MVSBGZBN005NUW0** – Run full test suite validation (parent AC5) (blocked)
- **MS-0MVRNW8PA000O6R5** – Competitive summary docs and suite (blocked)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: 0mvcrgkzy007died, 0mvo268500071bpi, ac4, ac5, acceptance (+482 more)
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: acceptance, actually, add, advance, advances (+370 more)
- `docs/dev/testing.md` — matched: 0mvo26g5h0054snv, ac1, ac3, ac4, acceptance (+326 more)

# Phaser 4 + WebGL: `GeometryMask` `setMask` is a no-op, so the street map and log viewports are unclipped

Discovered-from: MS-0MVRDVVH4001048Q (reputation crowd regression diagnosis, MS-0MVRMHS4S0067RRQ).

## Problem

The game runs Phaser `4.0.0-rc.7`. In Phaser 4 the WebGL renderer no longer supports `GameObject.setMask` with a `GeometryMask`; it logs and returns immediately:

```js
// node_modules/phaser/src/gameobjects/components/Mask.js
setMask: function (mask) {
    if (this.scene.renderer.type === CONST.WEBGL) {
        console.warn('Phaser.GameObjects.Components.Mask.setMask: This method is not supported in WebGL. Create a Mask filter instead.');
        return this;
    }
```

Observed on every street refresh of the real scene (WebGL, normal play):

```
Phaser.GameObjects.Components.Mask.setMask: This method is not supported in WebGL. Create a Mask filter instead.
```

Call sites in this repo that therefore do nothing under WebGL:

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts:611` — `s.streetContainer.setMask(mask)` (the street map viewport mask, `installStreetMapMask` / `updateStreetMapMask`)
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts:331` — `s.logContentContainer.setMask(s.logContentMask)` (Activity Log scroll clipping)
- `src/gym/GymCardIndexScene.ts:373` — `this.listContainer.setMask(this.listMask.createGeometryMask())` (card-index list clipping; `clearMask` at ~683)
- core (out of this repo): `core/src/ui/HelpPanel.ts:524`, `core/src/ui/Overlay.ts:484`, `core/src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts:909` — routed to `MS-0MVTE0UP00013TNW`

Consequences in a WebGL boot: the street map is no longer clipped to the street viewport (it can draw over neighbouring panels/outside its band), and the Activity Log / card-index list content is no longer clipped to its scroll area. The Canvas path (used by most browser tests) still honours the masks, so the regression is invisible to the test suite.

### Which renderer actually boots (verified 2026-10-29, plan)

The defect is **latent in the shipped launcher build and live in any WebGL boot**:

- `index.html` loads `/main.ts` (the scaffolded launcher entry), which calls `createCardGame({ …, type: Phaser.CANVAS })` — the packaged game is Canvas, so the masks still work there.
- `src/main.ts` (the standalone game entry) calls `createMainStreetGameWithPacks()` → `createCardGame` whose default is `type: renderType ?? Phaser.AUTO` (`core/src/ui/createCardGame.ts:123`) — that is WebGL on any GPU-capable browser.
- `tests/main-street/hud-total-counting-live.browser.test.ts:46` boots `createMainStreetGame()` with **no** `type`, i.e. AUTO → WebGL, so the warning path is already reachable from the test suite.

So this is a real defect that blocks/degrades the WebGL renderer (`MS-0MV1HJ9ES009Y8GK`), not a cosmetic log line.

## Plan (approved by producer 2026-10-29)

Producer decisions:

- **Q1 (priority/sequencing):** keep `medium`; this item is sequenced **before** `MS-0MV1HJ9ES009Y8GK` (dependency edge added) because it establishes that item's AC2 pattern.
- **Q2 (core-owned sites):** raise a core work item and record the deferral here → `MS-0MVTE0UP00013TNW`. The `core` submodule is not edited from this repo.
- **Q3 (scope):** **fold in** `src/gym/GymCardIndexScene.ts` (now AC3).
- **Q4 (approach):** **spike approved** as the first child, before the main implementation slice.

Children (test-first order; see the child items for their own ACs):

1. **Spike: WebGL container-clip approach** — decide and evidence the clipping mechanism (Mask filter on a `Container`, else a dedicated camera viewport). No production code.
2. **WebGL clipping regression test (red first)** — browser test on the real scene with `type: Phaser.WEBGL`: no `setMask … not supported in WebGL` warning, street content clipped to `streetViewportRect`, log content clipped, plus the Canvas parity check.
3. **Street map viewport clip under WebGL** — renderer-branched clip for `streetContainer`, Canvas path untouched.
4. **Activity Log scroll clip under WebGL** — renderer-branched clip for `logContentContainer`, reconciled with the existing per-entry visibility safety net.
5. **Gym card-index list clip under WebGL** — renderer-branched clip for `listContainer` (folded-in scope).
6. **Docs: renderer-dependent clipping + core deferral record** — `src/README.md`, `docs/dev/testing.md`, and the deferred core sites.

Between phases: re-read the next child's description and update it with what the previous phase learned (especially the spike's chosen mechanism).

## Notes / scope

- Not the cause of the crowd regression: an unclipped container renders *more*, not less, and the crowd was verified present, attached, textured and on-screen under WebGL (see `tests/main-street/pedestrians-scene-visibility.browser.test.ts`).
- Fix direction: Phaser 4 mask **filters** (`FilterList.addMask` / `Phaser.Filters.Mask`) for the WebGL path, or a renderer-agnostic clipping approach; verify visually in the real WebGL build and keep the Canvas behaviour unchanged.
- **Risky assumption (unproven in rc.7):** `addMask` lives on `Phaser.GameObjects.Components.FilterList`, which `Container` does *not* mix in (`node_modules/phaser/src/gameobjects/container/Container.js` mixes in `Mask`, `Transform`, `Visible`, … but not `FilterList`); `Container` does inherit the `Filters` component from `GameObject`. Applying a Mask filter to a `Container` (or `streetContainer` / `logContentContainer` specifically) is therefore **unverified** — this is what child 1 (the approved spike) resolves. Fallbacks, in preference order: per-camera viewport clipping (a dedicated camera whose viewport is the street band / log content rect), restructuring the clipped content into a filtered `Layer`, or an explicit scissor/`setCrop`-style renderer hook.
- **Partial mitigation already present:** `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts:814-830` hides log children whose local Y falls outside the visible window as a "safety net" for the unreliable GeometryMask clip. That hides fully-outside entries but cannot clip a partially-visible entry, so AC2 still stands.
- Canvas behaviour must not change: the GeometryMask path is correct under Canvas and is what the current test suite exercises. Prefer a renderer-branch (`scene.renderer.type === Phaser.WEBGL`) over a wholesale replacement so Canvas output stays byte-stable.
- Not in scope: the GPU card shader (`MS-0MUWNTQ5L0075Y38`) and the renderer switch itself.

### Related work (partial overlap — split of responsibilities)

- `MS-0MV1HJ9ES009Y8GK` — "Migrate Main Street renderer from Canvas to WebGL" (open, `plan_complete`, priority low). Its AC2 covers the *whole* GeometryMask → Mask-filter migration (core UI, gym scenes, Main Street) and its AC3 covers *creating* a WebGL browser-test project; both overlap this item. **Scope split:** this item owns the in-repo viewport-clipping defect (street map + Activity Log + gym card index) and the console-warning regression assertions; `MS-0MV1HJ9ES009Y8GK` owns the launcher/core boot switch, the core-owned call sites, and the general WebGL test-project plumbing. The pattern established here is the reference implementation for that item's AC2, and this item is a declared prerequisite of it.
- `MS-0MVTE0UP00013TNW` — core-owned `setMask` sites (HelpPanel / Overlay / SettingsPanel); deferred, cross-repo.
- `MS-0MVRDVVH4001048Q` / `MS-0MVRMHTW6006KQKI` — the crowd regression this was discovered from (diagnosis complete; guard landed).
- `MS-0MV14JDUG000E1V6` — Activity Log rendering (completed); relevant to the log-viewport clip.
- Duplicate check performed (`wl search "mask webgl"`, `"GeometryMask clipping"`) — no completed item already satisfies these ACs; overlap with `MS-0MV1HJ9ES009Y8GK` is partial only (see above).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The street map viewport is clipped to `streetViewportRect` in the real WebGL renderer (no rendering outside the band; map scroll/zoom still clipped as before).
2. The Activity Log content is clipped to its scroll area under WebGL.
3. The Gym card-index list is clipped to its list bounds under WebGL (`src/gym/GymCardIndexScene.ts`, `applyScroll`), including correct mask teardown in `cleanup()`.
4. No `setMask … not supported in WebGL` console warning remains in a real-scene WebGL boot of either scene (assert in browser tests on the real WebGL renderer).
5. Canvas rendering behaviour and the existing layout/panel tests stay green; the full suite passes.
6. Core-owned call sites are routed to the core work item `MS-0MVTE0UP00013TNW` and explicitly documented as deferred here.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — street map mask (`installStreetMapMask`/`updateStreetMapMask`, ~line 611) and log mask (~line 331) call sites
- `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — `logContentMask` / `streetMapMaskGraphics` field declarations (~line 257)
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` — log-scroll safety net (~line 814) that interacts with the log clip; also the `updateLogMask` caller
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` / `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererContext.ts` — mask install/update wiring
- `src/gym/GymCardIndexScene.ts` — third in-repo `setMask` site (`applyScroll`, ~line 373; `clearMask` ~line 683) — folded into scope (AC3)
- `src/MainStreetMapView.ts` — `streetViewportRect` (the rect the clip must match)
- `tests/main-street/pedestrians-scene-visibility.browser.test.ts` — real-scene boot harness to model the new WebGL test on (note: it boots `Phaser.CANVAS`, it is **not** an existing WebGL harness)
- `tests/main-street/hud-total-counting-live.browser.test.ts` — the only existing test that boots the real scene without a `type`, i.e. AUTO → WebGL; the natural place (or template) for the console-warning assertion in AC4
- `tests/main-street/GymCardIndexScene.browser.test.ts` — existing gym scene browser harness to extend for AC3
- `vite.config.ts` — `browser` project configuration (shared headless-Chromium context) if a WebGL boot needs launch args
- `src/README.md` — the "Viewport clipping" bullet (~line 105) currently states the street layer *is* clipped by a `GeometryMask`; must describe the renderer-dependent behaviour
- `docs/dev/testing.md` — browser-project conventions; note how to boot a WebGL browser test
- `docs/dev/` — no dedicated renderer doc exists today; add the Phaser 4 WebGL mask restriction note here (or in `src/README.md`) so the next reader does not repeat the diagnosis

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Recorded during the plan session (2026-10-29). Facts verified directly against the checkout; producer decisions are recorded below.

- Q: Is the reported defect reproducible in the shipped build? — Answer (code, verified): partly. The launcher entry (`index.html` → `main.ts`) boots `Phaser.CANVAS`, so the packaged game is unaffected; `src/main.ts` and any `createMainStreetGame()` call without a `type` boot AUTO → WebGL, where `setMask` is a no-op. Evidence: `main.ts:23`, `src/main.ts:16`, `core/src/ui/createCardGame.ts:123`, `tests/main-street/hud-total-counting-live.browser.test.ts:46`.
- Q: Does an existing WebGL browser-test harness exist to extend for the warning assertion? — Answer (code, verified): no. Every `*.browser.test.ts` that passes a renderer passes `Phaser.CANVAS` (77 call sites); `hud-total-counting-live.browser.test.ts` is the sole AUTO boot. The warning assertion therefore needs a new (or newly-WebGL-ified) browser test.
- Q: Is there already a planned item covering the GeometryMask migration? — Answer (code/wl, verified): yes, partially — `MS-0MV1HJ9ES009Y8GK` AC2/AC3. Scope split recorded under "Related work".
- Q: **OPEN QUESTION 1 (producer, priority/urgency)** — stay `medium` and sequence before `MS-0MV1HJ9ES009Y8GK`, or raise to `high`? — **Answer (producer, 2026-10-29): "as recommended"** → stay `medium`, sequenced before the migration item (dependency edge added). Final: medium, prerequisite of `MS-0MV1HJ9ES009Y8GK`.
- Q: **OPEN QUESTION 2 (producer, scope of AC5)** — raise a core work item and document the deferral, or authorise a core-repo session? — **Answer (producer, 2026-10-29): "as recommended"** → core work item raised as `MS-0MVTE0UP00013TNW`; deferral documented in AC6. Final: routed, deferred.
- Q: **OPEN QUESTION 3 (producer, scope)** — fold `src/gym/GymCardIndexScene.ts` in, or split it out? — **Answer (producer, 2026-10-29): "fold in"** → now AC3 plus child 5. Final: in scope.
- Q: **OPEN QUESTION 4 (engineering, approach)** — is a Phaser 4 `Mask` filter usable on a `Container` in rc.7? — **Answer (producer, 2026-10-29): "approve spike"** → child 1 (spike) runs first and records the chosen mechanism (Mask filter, else per-camera viewport clipping) before the implementation slice. Final: spike approved, approach decided by evidence.
